o1.biggest_strength: It gives the right straight answer on the 20% cut, uses the LTV and top-20 math well, and makes the credit-window and payout fixes the first moves.
o1.biggest_mistake: The cost estimate for giving Partners 40% in year one is a bit shaky and could understate the finance impact because it applies lifetime/new-customer logic to last-12-month revenue.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the Partner-tier cost model and add a clearer cap or pilot so finance can approve the 40% first-year tier with confidence.

o2.biggest_strength: It clearly rejects the 20% cut with the right LTV math and focuses attention on faster payouts, better attribution, and the active creator-educator partners.
o2.biggest_mistake: It is a little too cautious on the credit window and tiers, giving most affiliates only 60 days even though the data says the 30-day window is a core reason partners lose credit.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make 90-day attribution the standard plan, sharpen the top-20 treatment, and remove or better substantiate the speculative $38,000 new-customer-only savings point.

reason: Both are strong and usable, but Output 1 feels more like the programme redesign I asked for: it acts on the top-20 signal, fixes attribution and payouts fast, and gives a fuller one-plan structure. Output 2 is safer and very clear, but it underplays the 90-day credit fix and the tier design.
